records.independentlyDerivedAnswer: A: The longitudinal trapezium has area (1 + 3.5) / 2 × 6 = 13.5 m²; multiplying by the 5 m width gives 67.5 m³.
records.difficultyReason: Identify the sloping-bottom pool as a prism with a trapezium cross-section and choose the 6 m perpendicular separation rather than the 6.5 m sloping floor; then apply the taught cross-section area and prism volume methods. The multiple-choice options do not supply the decomposition.

The hardest essential parts require interpreting the 1 m clearance as a radius increment for the entire excavation and modelling rainfall as a shallow volume, including converting mm to metres and cubic metres to litres. The sprinkler division is direct; the separate parts are not averaged.

records.independentlyDerivedAnswer: B: Exact fit gives cylinder radius 6 cm and height 2 × 12 = 24 cm. Its volume is π × 6² × 24 = 864π ≈ 2,714 cm³.
records.difficultyReason: Exact fit must be translated into the cylinder radius of half one sphere diameter and a height of two diameters before applying the taught cylinder volume formula and rounding. Choosing the container rather than the spheres is explicit in the prompt.
